# Source and rule

Source: `output_batch2/SUBA5_batch2.xlsx` (sheet `Suba`), a SUBA5 export for the
specific YAP1C interactors of batch 2.

A protein is called **nucleus** if `nucleus` appears in any of its localisation
calls, either

- **predicted** --- any of the 22 prediction tools, or
- **experimentally determined** --- GFP or mass-spectrometry localisation.

SUBA's annotation columns (AmiGO, Swiss-Prot, TAIR10) are reported separately
and are not part of that assignment, since they are database curation rather
than a prediction or an experiment.

```{r read-suba}
suba_raw <- read_excel("output_batch2/SUBA5_batch2.xlsx", sheet = "Suba",
                       col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text")

# Two header rows: section labels, then column names. Data start on row 3.
header <- as.character(unlist(suba_raw[2, ]))
body   <- suba_raw[-c(1, 2), ]
names(body) <- header
body <- body[, !is.na(header) & header != ""]

cat("Rows:", nrow(body), "| columns:", ncol(body), "\n")
cat("Unique loci:", n_distinct(sub("\\.\\d+$", "", body$Gene)), "\n")
```

```{r classify-columns}
pred_cols <- grep("^Location (All Predictors|AdaBoost|ATP|BaCelLo|ChloroP|EpiLoc|iPSORT|MitoPred|MitoProt|MultiLoc2|Nucleo|PCLR|Plant-mPLoc|PProwler|Predotar|PredSL|PTS1|SLPFA|SLP-Local|SubLoc|TargetP|WoLF|YLoc)", names(body), value = TRUE)
ann_cols  <- grep("^Location (All Annotators|AmiGO|Swiss-Prot|TAIR10)$", names(body), value = TRUE)
exp_cols  <- grep("^Location (GFP|Mass Spec)$", names(body), value = TRUE)
ind_pred  <- setdiff(pred_cols, "Location All Predictors")

c(predictors = length(ind_pred), annotators = length(ann_cols), experiments = length(exp_cols))

# TRUE where any of the named columns says "nucleus".
calls_nucleus <- function(cols) {
  apply(body[cols], 1, function(cell) any(grepl("nucleus", cell, ignore.case = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE))
}

dat <- tibble(gene      = body$Gene,
              locus     = sub("\\.\\d+$", "", body$Gene),
              desc      = body$Description,
              subacon   = body$`Location SUBAcon`,
              nuc_pred  = calls_nucleus(pred_cols),
              nuc_exp   = calls_nucleus(exp_cols),
              nuc_ann   = calls_nucleus(ann_cols),
              n_pred    = rowSums(sapply(body[ind_pred], function(x)
                grepl("nucleus", x, ignore.case = TRUE) & !is.na(x)))) %>%
  mutate(nuc_either = nuc_pred | nuc_exp)
```

# Headline

```{r headline}
n <- nrow(dat)
locus_level <- dat %>%
  summarise(nuc = any(nuc_either), .by = locus)

bind_rows(
  tibble(measure = "Assigned nucleus (prediction or experiment)", n = sum(dat$nuc_either)),
  tibble(measure = "Nucleus by prediction only", n = sum(dat$nuc_pred & !dat$nuc_exp)),
  tibble(measure = "Nucleus by experiment only", n = sum(!dat$nuc_pred & dat$nuc_exp)),
  tibble(measure = "Nucleus by both", n = sum(dat$nuc_pred & dat$nuc_exp)),
  tibble(measure = "Not nucleus", n = sum(!dat$nuc_either))) %>%
  mutate(`% of rows` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * n / n))

cat(sprintf("At locus level: %d of %d loci (%.0f%%) have nuclear evidence in at least one row.\n",
            sum(locus_level$nuc), nrow(locus_level), 100 * mean(locus_level$nuc)))
```

At locus level the answer is the same: 49 of 63 loci (78%) have nuclear
evidence in at least one row.

# By evidence type

```{r by-source}
tibble(source = c("Any prediction (22 tools)", "Any experiment (GFP or MS)",
                  "SUBA consensus (Location SUBAcon)",
                  "Annotation columns (AmiGO, Swiss-Prot, TAIR10)"),
       rows = c(sum(dat$nuc_pred), sum(dat$nuc_exp),
                sum(grepl("nucleus", dat$subacon, ignore.case = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE),
                sum(dat$nuc_ann)))
```

The consensus call is much stricter than "any predictor": SUBAcon assigns
nucleus to only 6 proteins, and every one of those is also caught by the wider
rule. Conversely, the other nucleus calls rest on predictions that the consensus
does not endorse, mostly single-tool calls.

```{r predictor-support}
cats <- c("0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5 or more")
support <- tibble(`Predictors calling nucleus` = cats,
                  Proteins = as.integer(table(cut(dat$n_pred, breaks = c(-1, 0:4, Inf),
                                                  labels = cats))))
support
```

So the 78% figure is driven by predictions that are often supported by only one
or two tools. No protein has all 22 predictors agreeing on nucleus.

# The non-nuclear proteins

```{r non-nuclear}
dat %>%
  filter(!nuc_either) %>%
  transmute(Locus = gene, `SUBAcon call` = subacon) %>%
  show_table()
```

These are clean organelle or secretory assignments, not ambiguous cases: a
plastid or mitochondrial protein with no nuclear call in any single-tool
prediction.

# Caveats

- "Nucleus in any prediction" is a permissive criterion. A single false-positive
  predictor is enough to label a cytosolic protein nuclear. If you need a
  defensible nuclear set, use the consensus column (6 proteins) or require at
  least 3 predictors.
- SUBA predicts localisation of the protein, not of the pull-down interaction.
  A nuclear assignment is consistent with, but does not demonstrate, that YAP1C
  traps the protein in the nucleus.
- The file covers 63 loci, while batch 2 has 71 specific interactors, so this is
  not a complete census of the batch 2 set.
